jurisdiction.name: Iceland
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Iceland governs AI through its non-binding 2021 national AI strategy and the AI Action Plan 2025-2027 led by the Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education. The Data Protection Act 2018, which implements the GDPR and regulates automated decisions, is the only binding layer. The EU AI Act still awaits incorporation into the EEA Agreement and a national bill, and an October 2026 expert working-group report is shaping an updated plan due at the end of 2026. Iceland is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108), but its 1991 ratification act is not in the online gazette.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Culture, Innovation and Higher Education
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official gazette, the government consultation portal and the Government Offices' website; a run cut off by a usage limit was resumed and its downloads re-checked against the official texts. Parliament's website (althingi.is) could not be accessed, so bills before Parliament, including the planned AI Act bill, could not be checked. The data protection authority's AI guidance pages carry no date and are tracked as leads, together with the October 2026 working-group report.

instruments.current_status: Published July 2025 (document imprint 'Júlí 2025'; the Government's English report page dates it 1 July 2025); an official English version is published on the same Government site. The plan runs for two years from publication with six-monthly reviews and a full review by mid-2027. On 9 October 2026 the ministry stated that an updated AI and language-technology action plan is being prepared for release at the end of 2026, taking into account the 2026 working-group report (see leads). A draft titled 'Aðgerðaáætlun um gervigreind 2024-2026' was consulted on 7-21 Nov 2024 (Samráðsgátt case 223/2024).
instruments.summary: Iceland's government action plan on AI, built on the 2021 national AI strategy, with 20 actions under five pillars: AI for everyone, a competitive economy, education, public services and the future health system. Action 2 commits the ministry to assess the adaptation needed for incorporating the EU AI Act into the EEA Agreement and to prepare a bill on AI (including which institutions will have roles) by spring 2026; action 16 commits to an updated central set of guidelines for public bodies' use of AI, including on procurement of AI solutions, by spring 2027. Other actions cover an Icelandic AI and language-technology centre, joining the Nordic-Baltic AI centre, AI infrastructure, a national data strategy, AI in schools and health-data policy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI action plan; sets the roadmap for AI Act implementation and public-sector AI guidelines.

instruments.current_status: Published April 2021 by the Prime Minister's Office (date as printed in the document); still listed as Iceland's AI strategy on the Government's AI page (October 2026). The 2025-2027 Action Plan states that the strategy is due for revision alongside the plan's implementation. A first outline was consulted on 1-15 March 2021 (Samráðsgátt case 64/2021).
instruments.summary: Iceland's first national AI strategy, prepared by a committee for the Prime Minister's Office. Its stated goal is for Iceland to have a strong, shared ethical foundation for developing and using AI, grounded in knowledge of the technology and its security challenges; it discusses accountability, access, information and transparency, the regulatory environment for AI and Iceland's competitiveness, and sets objectives in areas such as education, democracy, human rights and research. It is non-binding and is implemented through the 2025-2027 AI Action Plan.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Foundational national AI strategy and ethical framework.

instruments.english_title: Act No. 90/2018 on Data Protection and the Processing of Personal Data
instruments.current_status: In force. Published in Stjórnartíðindi A-deild on 28 June 2018 (signed 27 June 2018); art. 53: the Act enters into force on 15 July 2018 and repeals Act No. 77/2000. Amendments after 2018 were not reviewed (consolidated text on althingi.is could not be accessed).
instruments.summary: Iceland's general data protection act, which incorporates the GDPR into Icelandic law and governs the processing of personal data, including for training and using AI systems. Art. 22 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects; the Act also defines profiling and sets the Data Protection Authority's (Persónuvernd) supervisory powers. It binds all controllers and processors in Iceland.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rules on automated decision-making and profiling; legal basis for the Data Protection Authority's AI guidance.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: National sources in Iceland were searched, including the official gazette, the consultation portal, government AI pages, ministries and regulators. No qualifying material was found for risk and assurance, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indexes, generative AI, drafts, international instruments or historical documents. leads.note: Expert working-group report (69 proposals in ten areas, incl. AI Act/legal framework, public-sector use, education) presented to the Government; announced 9 Oct 2026 at https://www.stjornarradid.is/efst-a-baugi/frettir/stok-frett/2026-10-09-skyrsla-starfshops-um-malefni-gervigreindar/ with PDF https://www.stjornarradid.is/library?itemid=ccb3cdc0-5eb4-4054-ba1c-37dce279dded&type=pdf (read). Advisory recommendations, not adopted policy; the same day the Government approved one proposal, a steering group of ministries on AI (no founding document found). Ministries will review the proposals and an updated AI and language-technology action plan is planned for end of 2026. Promote the steering group / updated plan once documents are published.
